The two stances genuinely contradict: Anthropic says the agent has its OWN service-account identity ('Claude isn't acting on behalf of a single user'); Kenton says ALL agent authority must DERIVE from a specific human for accountability ('Claude acting on behalf of Bob deleted the database') and 'Bob must not command Alice's agent with Alice's credentials'. AGP already aligns with Kenton on accountability (every require-verdict routes to a HUMAN approver in Slack; the signed journal records the approval) but has not taken an explicit position on the authority-derivation model, and the deferred hosted multi-tenant work (047-AT-ADR gate; agp-pne prep CLOSED) is exactly where 'Bob commanding Alice's agent' becomes a live hole. CCSC substrate audit (2026-06-24) confirms the same gaps exist there by design: authority is host-UID-rooted not human-derived; one shared credential pool serves all Slack users; the journal actor is a 5-value role enum with NO per-human user_id/on_behalf_of; authorization is coarse allowlist membership; ownerId is creation-time-only with no speaker==owner recheck (CCSC THREAT-MODEL.md:519-529 names multi-user as a 'rewrite from principals up'; capability tokens ccsc-66t / ADR-001 are research-stage).
design: References: 047-AT-ADR (multi-tenant gate), 046-AT-ARCH (multi-tenant readiness), agp-pne (CLOSED prep epic), Anthropic 'Agent Identity and Access Model', Kenton Varda critique. Consider capability-based grant (task-derived capabilities) vs the current broad-sandbox + policy-gate model. The matching detailed GitHub issue is the reference artifact for future sessions.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision (AT-DECR or AT-ADR in 000-docs) BEFORE any hosted multi-tenant code, ruling on: (1) does AGP adopt human-derived authority (commanding human = principal) vs Anthropic agent-as-service-principal; (2) per-human credential scoping so Bob's commands use Bob's credential subset, never Alice's; (3) an explicit no-cross-user-command rule (speaker==owner recheck, or re-derive capabilities under the speaker's credentials); (4) whether the JournalEvent contract gains an on_behalf_of / principal-user field so 'which human' is answerable, not just 'a human approver'.
